Perfect! I now have a comprehensive overview. Let me compile my findings:

## CabinetMaker Solution - Complete Overview

### 1. Projects & Purpose

All projects target **.NET 10.0**:

- **CabinetMaker.Domain** - Domain entities and repository interfaces
- **CabinetMaker.Domain.Shared** - Shared settings, DTOs, and POCOs
- **CabinetMaker.DAL** - Data Access Layer with DbContext, migrations, and repositories
- **CabinetMaker.BRL** - Business Rules Layer with services and DI configuration
- **CabinetMaker.Web** - Blazor Server web application with Razor components and identity

### 2. Domain Entities (CabinetMaker.Domain/Entities)

**Core Base Classes:**
- `CmEntity` - Base class with audit fields: CreatedDate, CreatedUserId, LastUpdatedDate, LastUpdatedUserId, RecordStateId
- `CmEntityHistory` - Extends CmEntity, adds EffectiveDate, ObsoleteDate (for temporal records)
- `ITenantScoped` - Interface requiring TenantId (multi-tenancy support)
- `ITemporalRecord` - Interface for temporal data

**Dictionary/Reference Data:**
- `CmType` (TypeID, TypeClassID, Name, Description, Ordering, TypeInt, TypeString, TypeDecimal)
- `CmTypeClass` (CmTypeClassID, Name, Description, BaseTypeID, DefaultValue)
- `CmUnit` (UnitID, Name, Abbreviation, IsSystemBase, BaseMultiplier, DisplayPrecision, UnitTypeID)
- `CmMeasurement` (CmMeasurmentId, UnitId, RawValue, Unit navigation)

**Plans/Subscriptions:**
- `Plan` (PlanId, PlanGuid, Name, Slug, IsPubliclyVisible, SortOrder)
- `PlanDetail` (PlanDetailId, PlanDetailGuid, PlanId, DisplayName, Tagline, MonthlyPrice, AnnualPrice, PriceDisplayOverride) - extends CmEntityHistory

**Tenancy/Identity:**
- `Tenant` (TenantId, TenantGuid, Name, Slug, IsActive, PlanId)
- `TenantSettings` (TenantSettingsId, TenantSettingsGuid, TenantId, ShopHourlyRate, DefaultMarkupPercentage, DefaultMarginPercentage)
- `User` - Extends IdentityUser<int> (UserGuid, TenantId, DisplayName)
- `UserPreference` (UserPreferenceId, UserPreferenceGuid, UserId, PreferenceTypeId, TypeInt, TypeString, TypeDecimal)

**Contacts:**
- `Contact` (ContactId, ContactGuid, TenantId, Prefix, FirstName, LastName, Suffix) - implements ITenantScoped
- `ContactMethod` (ContactMethodId, ContactMethodGuid, ContactId, TenantId, ContactTypeId, ContactValue, PreferedContactMethod) - implements ITenantScoped
- `ContactNote` (ContactNoteId, ContactNoteGuid, ContactId, TenantId, Note) - extends CmEntityHistory, implements ITenantScoped

**Materials/Inventory:**
- `CmMaterial` (CmMaterialId)
- `CmMaterialDetail` (CmMaterialDetailId, Name, Description) - extends CmEntityHistory
- `CmMaterialAttribute` (CmMaterialAttributreId, CmMaterialId, AttributeTypeId, MeasurementId, StringValue, BoolValue)
- `MaterialTenantDetail` (MaterialTenantDetailId, MaterialTenantDetailGuid, TenantId, MaterialId, IsHidden, OverrideName, OverrideUnitCost, OverrideWasteFactorPercentage) - extends CmEntityHistory, implements ITenantScoped
- `MaterialTenantAttribute` (MaterialTenantAttributeId, MaterialTenantAttributeGuid, TenantId, MaterialId, AttributeTypeId, MeasurementId, StringValue, BoolValue) - extends CmEntityHistory, implements ITenantScoped

**Jobs & Assembly:**
- `Job` (JobId, JobGuid, TenantId, Name, ClientContactId, JobStatusTypeId, TargetDate, Notes) - implements ITenantScoped
- `CmAssembly` (AssemblyId, AssemblyGuid, TenantId, JobId, Name, OverallHeightMeasurementId, OverallWidthMeasurementId, OverallDepthMeasurementId) - implements ITenantScoped
- `Part` (PartId, PartGuid, TenantId, AssemblyId, Name, Quantity, CutLengthMeasurementId, CutWidthMeasurementId, MaterialId) - implements ITenantScoped
- `PartOperation` (PartOperationId, PartOperationGuid, TenantId, PartId, OperationTypeId, Face, OperationParametersJson) - implements ITenantScoped

**Estimates:**
- `JobEstimate` (JobEstimateId, JobEstimateGuid, TenantId, JobId, EstimateStatusTypeId, Version, GeneratedAt, SentAt, ShopHourlyRate, MarkupPercentage, TotalCost, Notes) - implements ITenantScoped
- `JobEstimateLine` (JobEstimateLineId, JobEstimateLineGuid, TenantId, JobEstimateId, PartId, TenantDiscountCodeId, LineTypeId, Description, Quantity, UnitCost, TotalCost, SortOrder) - implements ITenantScoped
- `TenantDiscountCode` (TenantDiscountCodeId, TenantDiscountCodeGuid, TenantId, Code, Description, DiscountTypeId, DiscountValue, ExpiresAt, MaxUses, UsageCount) - implements ITenantScoped

### 3. Pages/Components in CabinetMaker.Web

**Layout Components:**
- `App.razor` - Root component
- `MainLayout.razor` - Main layout wrapper
- `NavMenu.razor` - Navigation menu
- `ReconnectModal.razor` - Reconnection UI
- `Routes.razor` - Route configuration
- `_Imports.razor` - Global imports

**Pages:**
- `Home.razor` - Home page (minimal placeholder)
- `Error.razor` - Error page
- `NotFound.razor` - 404 page
- `AuthTest.razor` - Authorized test page

**Auth Components:**
- `RedirectToLogin.razor` - Login redirect handler
- `RedirectToUpgrade.razor` - Upgrade redirect handler
- `MfaReminder.razor` - MFA reminder component

**Account/Identity Pages (in Components/Account):**
- `Login.razor` - Login form
- `LoginMfa.razor` - MFA login
- `Manage/TwoFactorAuthentication.razor` - 2FA management
- `Manage/EnableAuthenticator.razor` - Authenticator setup
- `Manage/Disable2fa.razor` - Disable 2FA
- `Shared/StatusMessage.razor` - Status message display

### 4. Services & Repositories

**CabinetMaker.DAL:**
- **DbContext**: `CmContext` (/workspace/src/CabinetMaker.DAL/Context/CmContext.cs)
  - Extends IdentityDbContext<User, IdentityRole<int>, int>
  - 18 DbSets (see below)
  - UTC DateTime enforcement
  - Automatic audit field stamping (CreatedDate, LastUpdatedDate)
  
- **Repositories**: 
  - `IRepository<T>` interface - GetAsync, GetAsync(id), UpdateAsync, AddAsync, DeleteAsync (both overloads)
  - `BaseRepository<T>` - Implements IRepository (stub implementations)
  - `UnitRepository` - Extends BaseRepository<CmUnit>

**CabinetMaker.BRL:**
- `DbSeeder` - Seeds roles (Admin, TenantAdmin, User) and admin user
- Extension classes for DI configuration

### 5. DbContext DbSets (CmContext)

```
// Dictionary & Units
Types, TypeClasses, Units, Measurements

// Plans
Plans, PlanDetails, PlanAttributes

// Identity & Tenancy
Tenants, TenantSettings, UserPreferences

// Contacts
Contacts, ContactMethods, ContactNotes

// Materials
Materials, MaterialDetails, MaterialAttributes, 
MaterialTenantDetails, MaterialTenantAttributes

// Jobs & Assemblies
Jobs, Assemblies, Parts, PartOperations

// Estimates
JobEstimates, JobEstimateLines, DiscountCodes
```

**Total: 21 DbSets**

### 6. Shared Configuration

**CabinetMaker.Domain.Shared:**
- `CmSettings` - Root config (DatabaseProvider, ConnectionStrings, Seed config)
- `CmDbSettings` - Database connection settings
- `CmSeedSettings` - Seed data config (AdminEmail, AdminPassword, AdminDisplayName)
- `CmTypePoco` - DTO for CmType with navigation data
- `UserSummaryPoco` - User summary DTO

### Technology Stack
- **Framework**: .NET 10.0, Blazor Server
- **ORM**: Entity Framework Core 10.0.12
- **Identity**: ASP.NET Core Identity
- **Database**: MySQL (primary), SQL Server support
- **Mapping**: Riok.Mapperly 4.3.1
- **Other**: QRCoder 1.4.3 (for 2FA QR codes)

---
name: Soft delete pattern
description: Never hard-delete records; always soft-delete via RecordStateId on CmEntity
type: feedback
---

Never use hard deletes (Remove/Delete from DbContext). Every entity extends CmEntity which has RecordStateId. A "delete" means setting RecordStateId = (int)RecordStateTypeId.Deleted and calling UpdateAsync.

**Why:** The DB design is built around record lifecycle — Active (1000), Deleted (1001), Archived (1002). Hard deletes destroy audit history and break referential integrity across the temporal data model.

**How to apply:** In BaseRepository.DeleteAsync, set RecordStateId to Deleted and call UpdateAsync. GetAllAsync and GetAsync(predicate) always filter to RecordStateId == Active only.

content.content:
1	# CabinetMaker — Project Plan
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-10-10
4	
5	**Stack:** C# · Blazor Server · .NET 10 · Entity Framework Core 10 · MySQL (primary) / SQL Server (supported) · Bootstrap · Docker (Linux)
6	
7	## 1. Project Purpose
8	
9	CabinetMaker is a professional-grade, multi-tenant design tool for cabinet makers and furniture builders. Its core job is to capture, organize, and calculate measurements for cabinet projects — from a single unit to a complete kitchen or custom furniture piece — and produce accurate cut lists, material estimates, and project summaries.
10	
11	Two foundational primitives underpin everything else:
12	
13	1. A **database-driven, unit-agnostic measurement system** — every dimension, mass, or volume flows through a unified conversion engine, preventing metric/imperial collisions and supporting tape-measure-accurate fractional snapping.
14	
15	2. A **tenant isolation model** — every piece of data is scoped to the tenant it belongs to, enforced at the database layer, invisible to application code.
16	
17	## 2. Infrastructure & Deployment
18	
19	### 2.1 Docker / Linux Hosting
20	
21	The application is packaged as a Docker container and can run on any Linux Docker host (self-hosted, VPS, cloud VM). No Azure-specific or Windows-specific dependencies are permitted.
22	
23	```
24	docker-compose.yml (development)
25	  web       — CabinetMaker.Web container (port 8080)
26	  db        — MySQL 8.x container (port 3306)
27	
28	Dockerfile  (multi-stage)
29	  Stage 1 (build): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0
30	  Stage 2 (runtime): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-bookworm-slim
31	```
32	
33	All configuration (connection strings, admin seed credentials) is supplied via environment variables. No secrets are baked into the image.
34	
35	Two compose files are maintained:
36	
37	| File | Purpose |
38	|---|---|
39	| `docker-compose.yml` | Local development — builds from source, exposes all ports, ships with safe dev defaults, includes dbgate DB admin UI on port 8081 |
40	| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | Production — pulls a pre-built registry image, binds web to `127.0.0.1:8080` only, no default passwords, `restart: always`, no DB admin UI |
41	
42	### 2.1.1 Production Reverse Proxy
43	
44	In production the app sits behind an existing nginx reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager or equivalent). The app container binds only to `127.0.0.1:8080` — it is never directly internet-facing. The proxy handles SSL termination, domain assignment, and certificate management. Deploying a new version is: push image to registry → pull on server → `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d` → register the `127.0.0.1:8080` upstream in the proxy console. No nginx container is included in the production compose file.
45	
46	### 2.2 Database Provider Abstraction
47	
48	**Primary: MySQL 8.x** (Oracle official `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` provider). **Also supported: SQL Server** (Microsoft EF Core provider). The active provider is selected at startup from a single config value:
49	
50	```
51	# appsettings.json / environment variable
52	"DatabaseProvider": "MySql"   // or "SqlServer"
53	```
54	
55	A `DatabaseProviderFactory` extension method in DAL registers the correct `DbContextOptions` based on this value:
56	
57	```csharp
58	// DAL/Extensions/DatabaseProviderExtensions.cs
59	services.AddDbContext<CabinetMakerDbContext>(options =>
60	{
61	    if (provider == "MySql")
62	        options.UseMySQL(connectionString);
63	    else
64	        options.UseSqlServer(connectionString);
65	});
66	```
67	
68	**Provider differences to account for:**
69	
70	| Feature | MySQL (Pomelo) | SQL Server |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| JSON columns | `JSON` type, `.HasColumnType("json")` | `nvarchar(max)` or `json` (SQL Server 2022+) |
73	| GUIDs | `char(36)` or `binary(16)` | `uniqueidentifier` |
74	| Auto-increment | `AUTO_INCREMENT` | `IDENTITY` |
75	| Migrations | Separate migration sets per provider, or provider-aware migrations |
76	
77	Migrations are kept in separate folders: `DAL/Migrations/MySql/` and `DAL/Migrations/SqlServer/`. A CLI helper script selects the correct migration context at design time.
78	
79	### 2.3 Timezone Architecture
80	
81	All temporal data in the system must be unambiguous about which instant in time it refers to. This matters especially for future-dated succession records (§5.1) where a user schedules a material change to take effect "at midnight on Nov 1" — midnight in *whose* timezone needs a definitive answer.
82	
83	#### Rule: UTC everywhere in the database and server
84	
85	- **Database:** All `DATETIME` columns store UTC values. The DB server timezone is irrelevant and must never influence stored values. MySQL `TIMESTAMP` type is specifically avoided because it auto-converts using the server timezone — `DATETIME` is used instead.
86	- **C# domain model:** All temporal properties use `DateTime`, always in UTC. The convention is enforced at the service boundary — every value written to a `DateTime` field must be UTC. Reading from DB always returns UTC. `DateTime.Now` is never used anywhere in the codebase.
87	- **EF Core convention:** A global value converter enforces `DateTimeKind.Utc` on all `DateTime` properties at the DbContext boundary, converting any non-UTC value on read and throwing on write if `Kind != Utc`.
88	- **Server-side "now":** All services obtain the current instant through an injected `TimeProvider`. Never call `DateTime.UtcNow` or `DateTime.Now` directly.
89	
90	```csharp
91	// Production — registered once in Program.cs
92	services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);
93	
94	// In any service that needs the current time
95	public class RecordSuccessionService(TimeProvider timeProvider)
96	{
97	    private DateTime Now => _timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime;
98	}
99	```
100	
101	Using `TimeProvider` makes every service that touches time fully testable — `FakeTimeProvider` (from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`) lets tests set and advance the clock without any static manipulation.
102	
103	#### Rule: User timezone stays in the UI layer
104	
105	The server and BRL services are timezone-unaware. They only speak UTC. Conversion happens at the edges:
106	
107	```
108	User types "Nov 1 midnight"
109	  → UI reads user's IANA timezone from preference (e.g., "America/New_York")
110	  → UI converts: Nov 1 00:00 America/New_York → 2026-11-01 05:00:00 UTC
111	  → Command sent to BRL carries the UTC DateTime
112	  → Stored in DB as UTC DATETIME
113	
114	DB returns 2026-11-01 05:00:00 (UTC)
115	  → UI converts back to America/New_York → displays "Nov 1 12:00 AM"
116	```
117	
118	#### User Timezone Preference
119	
120	Each `ApplicationUser` stores an IANA timezone identifier (e.g., `America/New_York`, `Europe/London`, `America/Los_Angeles`). Windows timezone names are explicitly not used — IANA identifiers are portable across Linux containers.
121	
122	If a user has not set a timezone preference, the Blazor app captures the browser's IANA timezone via a one-time JS interop call on session start and uses it as the session default (without persisting it):
123	
124	```javascript
125	// Called once on circuit connect
126	Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone  // → "America/Chicago"
127	```
128	
129	#### Timezone Conversion Service
130	
131	`ITimezoneService` is defined in BRL. The Web project provides the implementation using `NodaTime` (which correctly handles DST transitions, historical offset changes, and all IANA timezone rules):
132	
133	```csharp
134	public interface ITimezoneService
135	{
136	    DateTime ToUtc(DateTime localDateTime, string ianaTimezoneId);
137	    DateTime ToLocal(DateTime utcValue, string ianaTimezoneId);
138	    string GetUserTimezone(); // reads from current user claim or session default
139	}
140	```
141	
142	`NodaTime` is added only to the **Web** project (display concerns). Domain and BRL remain free of any NodaTime dependency — they only ever hold `DateTime` values in UTC.
143	
144	#### DST Transition Edge Cases
145	
146	DST transitions produce two distinct failure modes that require explicit handling. Both are **UI input problems only** — once a value is stored as UTC the succession logic is completely DST-immune.
147	
148	**Case 1 — Gap (spring forward):** Clocks jump forward (e.g., 2:00 AM → 3:00 AM on March 8 in US/Central). The hour 2:00–3:00 AM does not exist. Any local time in that window is invalid.
149	
150	**Case 2 — Overlap (fall back):** Clocks fall back (e.g., 2:00 AM → 1:00 AM on Nov 1 in US/Central). The hour 1:00–2:00 AM occurs twice. "1:30 AM Nov 1" is ambiguous — it could be 1:30 AM CDT (UTC−5) or 1:30 AM CST (UTC−6), two different UTC instants 60 minutes apart.
151	
152	NodaTime's `DateTimeZone.MapLocal(LocalDateTime)` returns a `ZoneLocalMapping` that explicitly identifies which case applies:
153	
154	```csharp
155	var zone = DateTimeZoneProviders.Tzdb[ianaTimezoneId];
156	var mapping = zone.MapLocal(localDateTime);
157	
158	switch (mapping.Count)
159	{
160	    case 1:
161	        // Unambiguous — normal case
162	        return mapping.Single().ToDateTimeUtc().ToDateTimeUnspecified(); // DateTime UTC
163	
164	    case 0:
165	        // GAP: this local time does not exist (spring forward)
166	        // Do not silently snap — surface to the user
167	        throw new SkippedTimeException(localDateTime, zone);
168	
169	    case 2:
170	        // OVERLAP: this local time exists twice (fall back)
171	        // Do not silently pick one — surface to the user
172	        throw new AmbiguousTimeException(localDateTime, zone,
173	            mapping.First().ToDateTimeUtc(),   // earlier (daylight) as UTC DateTime
174	            mapping.Last().ToDateTimeUtc());   // later (standard) as UTC DateTime
175	}
176	```
177	
178	**UI behavior for each case:**
179	
180	| Case | What the user sees | Suggested default |
181	|---|---|---|
182	| Normal | Nothing — input accepted, converted to UTC silently | — |
183	| Gap (spring forward) | Inline warning: *"This time doesn't exist — clocks skip from [before] to [after] on this date. Use [time before gap] or [time after gap]?"* with two buttons | Snap forward (post-gap) |
184	| Overlap (fall back) | Inline warning: *"This time occurs twice due to the clock change. Which did you mean — [offset 1] or [offset 2]?"* with two buttons showing explicit UTC offsets | Standard time (later occurrence) |
185	
186	Both warnings are handled in the `DateTimeInput` Blazor component. The component emits a resolved UTC `DateTime` only after the ambiguity is cleared.
187	
188	**Why succession records are DST-immune once stored:**
189	
190	The temporal query `EffectiveDate <= queryInstant && (ObsoleteDate == null || ObsoleteDate > queryInstant)` runs entirely in UTC. UTC has no clock changes — every instant is unique and unambiguous. No "blocking out" strategy is needed, unlike recurring scheduled tasks which must deal with DST on every firing.
191	
192	The recurring-scheduler problem arises because a rule like "run at 2:00 AM every day" has to be re-evaluated each day against a potentially shifting local clock. Succession records have no such rule — they are one-time point-in-time events fully resolved to UTC at the moment of creation.
193	
194	#### Why This Avoids the Common Pitfalls
195	
196	| Pitfall | How this design avoids it |
197	|---|---|
198	| Spring-forward gap: user enters a non-existent time | `ZoneLocalMapping.Count == 0` detected; UI shows disambiguation — never silently snapped |
199	| Fall-back overlap: user enters an ambiguous time | `ZoneLocalMapping.Count == 2` detected; UI shows both UTC offsets for user to choose |
200	| Recurring task fires twice on fall-back | Not applicable — successions are one-time events, not recurring rules |
201	| MySQL server timezone contamination | `DATETIME` type (not `TIMESTAMP`) — MySQL never auto-converts |
202	| `DateTime.Kind.Unspecified` written to DB | EF global value converter enforces `DateTimeKind.Utc` on all `DateTime` properties — throws on write if Kind is not Utc |
203	| Future date stored in wrong timezone | User input always converted to UTC in UI before leaving the browser context |
204	| Reporting across timezones | All report queries run in UTC; display layer converts per-user |
205	
206	## 3. Solution Structure
207	
208	```
209	CabinetMaker.slnx
210	└── src/
211	    ├── CabinetMaker.Domain/         # EF entities + base classes — private to DAL
212	    ├── CabinetMaker.Domain.Shared/  # POCOs, repository interfaces, Result<T>, Mapperly mappers
213	    ├── CabinetMaker.DAL/            # EF DbContext, migrations, repository implementations
214	    ├── CabinetMaker.BRL/            # Business rules, services, validation
215	    └── CabinetMaker.Web/            # Blazor Server UI, ViewModels (MVVM)
216	
217	# Future phase — added only when MAUI client is built:
218	#   CabinetMaker.API/               # GraphQL API (Hot Chocolate) — thin layer over BRL
219	#   CabinetMaker.MAUI/              # .NET MAUI client — calls API via GraphQL
220	```
221	
222	### Project Dependency Flow
223	
224	```
225	Web  ──────────────────────────────────► Domain.Shared
226	 │                                            ▲
227	 ▼                                            │
228	BRL  ──────────────────────────────────► Domain.Shared
229	 │                                            ▲
230	 ▼                                            │
231	DAL  ──► Domain (EF entities)  ──────► Domain.Shared
232	```
233	
234	| Project | References | Never references |
235	|---|---|---|
236	| `Domain` | *(none)* | Everything else |
237	| `Domain.Shared` | *(none)* | Everything else |
238	| `DAL` | `Domain` + `Domain.Shared` | `BRL`, `Web` |
239	| `BRL` | `Domain.Shared` only | `Domain`, `DAL` directly |
240	| `Web` | `BRL` + `Domain.Shared` | `Domain`, `DAL` directly |
241	
242	`Domain` is completely invisible above the DAL boundary. BRL and Web never import an EF entity type. DAL repositories accept and return only `Domain.Shared` POCOs — the EF entity is an internal implementation detail of the repository method.
243	
244	### What lives in each project
245	
246	**`Domain`** — EF entity classes, `CmEntity` / `CmEntityHistory` base classes. Nothing else.
247	
248	**`Domain.Shared`** — everything the upper layers need to work with:
249	- **POCOs** — plain classes mirroring entity data shapes, no base class, no EF attributes. **POCOs expose `{TableName}Guid` only — the `int {TableName}Id` is stripped at the DAL boundary and never reaches BRL or Web.** All POCO-to-POCO references use `Guid` properties.
250	- **Repository interfaces** — `IProjectRepository`, `IMaterialRepository`, etc.; all signatures use POCO types
251	- **Service interfaces** — `ITimezoneService`, `IPlanGateService`, etc.
252	- **`Result<T>`** — the success/failure discriminated union used throughout BRL
253	- **Shared enums** — `PlanFeature`, `RecordState`, `PlanType`
254	- **Mapperly POCO→POCO mappers** — for any cross-POCO transformations needed in BRL or Web
255	
256	**`DAL`** — EF `DbContext`, repository implementations, migrations, and **Mapperly Entity→POCO mappers**. This is the only project that ever sees both an EF entity and its POCO counterpart. The mapper runs just before a repository method returns.
257	
258	### Mapperly — Entity → POCO mapping
259	
260	[Mapperly](https://mapperly.riok.app/) (`Riok.Mapperly`) is a source generator: you declare a partial mapper class and it emits the full mapping method body at compile time. Zero reflection, no runtime overhead, and mapping errors surface at build time.
261	
262	```csharp
263	// DAL/Mappers/MaterialMapper.cs
264	[Mapper]
265	public partial class MaterialMapper
266	{
267	    public partial MaterialPoco ToMaterial(Material entity);
268	    public partial Material ToEntity(MaterialPoco poco);
269	
270	    // Collections handled automatically
271	    public partial List<MaterialPoco> ToMaterialList(IEnumerable<Material> entities);
272	}
273	```
274	
275	The mapper in DAL is also responsible for the int→Guid promotion: the entity carries both `{TableName}Id` and `{TableName}Guid`, but the generated POCO only receives the `Guid`. The `int` key never leaves the DAL.
276	
277	- Entity→POCO mappers live in **DAL** (only project with access to both types)
278	- POCO→POCO mappers (e.g., flattening for a report view) live in **Domain.Shared**
279	- Mapperly is added to **both** `Domain.Shared` and `DAL` as a source-generator-only reference:
280	
281	```xml
282	<PackageReference Include="Riok.Mapperly" Version="x.x.x"
283	                  PrivateAssets="all" IncludeAssets="analyzers;build" />
284	```
285	
286	`PrivateAssets="all"` means the generator runs at build time but adds no runtime DLL dependency — the output is just the generated C# code.
287	
288	## 4. Multi-Tenancy & Identity Architecture
289	
290	### 3.1 Isolation Model — Row-Level with Global Query Filters
291	
292	**Choice: single database, shared schema, `TenantId` discriminator column on every tenant-scoped table.**
293	EF Core Global Query Filters enforce isolation at the ORM layer. No query in the application ever accidentally crosses tenant boundaries.
294	
295	### 3.2 Base Classes & Key Naming Convention
296	
297	All entities inherit from one of two base classes defined in `CabinetMaker.Domain`:
298	
299	**`CmEntity`** — standard base for all non-temporal entities:
300	
301	```csharp
302	// CabinetMaker.Domain/Entities/CmEntity.cs
303	public class CmEntity
304	{
305	    public DateTime CreatedDate { get; set; }       // UTC — set on insert
306	    public int CreatedUserId { get; set; }          // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
307	    public DateTime? LastUpdatedDate { get; set; }  // UTC — set on every update
308	    public int? LastUpdatedUserId { get; set; }     // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
309	    public int RecordStateId { get; set; }          // FK → CmType (Active/Inactive/Deleted)
310	}
311	```
312	
313	**`CmEntityHistory`** — base for all temporal (succession-pattern) entities:
314	
315	```csharp
316	// CabinetMaker.Domain/Entities/CmEntityHistory.cs
317	public class CmEntityHistory : CmEntity
318	{
319	    public DateTime EffectiveDate { get; set; }     // UTC — when this record becomes active
320	    public DateTime? ObsoleteDate { get; set; }     // UTC — when this record is superseded
321	}
322	```
323	
324	All `DateTime` fields in both classes are **always UTC**. `DateTime.Now` and `DateTime.UtcNow` are never called directly — the current time is always obtained from an injected `TimeProvider` via `_timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime`.
325	
326	**Key naming on top of the base classes:**
327	
328	Every entity declares its own named PK and external Guid — the base class does not define them because the name must match the table:
329	
330	| Property | Type | Purpose |
331	|---|---|---|
332	| `{TableName}Id` | `int` (auto-increment PK) | Internal DB joins — never exposed in URLs or API responses |
333	| `{TableName}Guid` | `Guid` (unique index) | External identifier — used in all UI routes, links, and exports |
334	
335	`{TableName}Guid` is generated server-side (`Guid.NewGuid()`) in `SaveChangesAsync` on insert — never supplied by the client.
336	
337	### 3.3 Tenant-Scoped Entities
338	
339	Every entity that belongs to a tenant implements the marker interface. `TenantId` is an `int` FK to `Tenant.TenantId` — all joins use the int key, not the Guid.
340	
341	```csharp
342	public interface ITenantScoped
343	{
344	    int TenantId { get; set; }   // FK → Tenant.TenantId (int)
345	}
346	```
347	
348	Entities that are **not** tenant-scoped: `Tenant`, `ApplicationUser`, and System Dictionaries (`CmTypeClass`, `CmType`, `CmUnit`).
349	
350	### 3.3.1 ApplicationUser
351	
352	ASP.NET Core Identity does not allow renaming the `Id` property, so `ApplicationUser` is an exception to the `{TableName}Id` convention — it retains Identity's `int Id`. A `Guid ApplicationUserGuid` serves the same external-reference purpose.
353	
354	```csharp
355	public class ApplicationUser : IdentityUser<int>   // int PK via Identity
356	{
357	    public Guid UserGuid { get; set; }             // external reference
358	    public int? TenantId { get; set; }             // null = SystemAdmin; FK → Tenant.TenantId
359	    public string DisplayName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
360	}
361	```
362	
363	Display preferences (timezone, measurement units) live in `UserPreferences` — not on the Identity table.
364	
365	### 3.3.2 UserPreference
366	
367	A one-to-many collection of key-value preference rows per user. Adding a new preference type (theme, language, date format, etc.) requires only a new `CmType` seed record — no schema change ever needed.
368	
369	```csharp
370	public class UserPreference : CmEntity
371	{
372	    public int UserPreferenceId { get; set; }       // PK
373	    public Guid UserPreferenceGuid { get; set; }    // external reference
374	    public int UserId { get; set; }                 // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
375	    public int PreferenceTypeId { get; set; }       // FK → CmType (TimeZone / MeasurementUnit / Theme / etc.)
376	    public virtual CmType PreferenceType { get; set; } = null!;
377	    public int? TypeInt { get; set; }               // integer preference value
378	    public string? TypeString { get; set; }         // string preference value
379	    public decimal? TypeDecimal { get; set; }       // decimal preference value
380	}
381	```
382	
383	Each preference is one row. Examples:
384	
385	| `PreferenceType` (`CmType`) | Value field | Example value |
386	|---|---|---|
387	| `TimeZone` | `TypeString` | `"America/New_York"` |
388	| `MeasurementUnit` | `TypeInt` | CmUnitId for inches |
389	| `Theme` | `TypeString` | `"dark"` |
390	| `DateFormat` | `TypeString` | `"MM/dd/yyyy"` |
391	
392	At registration, `RegistrationService` seeds the two default rows (`TimeZone = "UTC"`, `MeasurementUnit = null` / system default). All preference rows for a user are loaded once at login and written as claims so the Web layer reads them without a DB hit per request:
393	
394	```csharp
395	foreach (var pref in userPreferences)
396	    claims.Add(new Claim($"pref_{pref.PreferenceType.Name}", pref.TypeString ?? pref.TypeInt?.ToString() ?? ""));
397	```
398	
399	### 3.4 User Signup & Tenant Auto-Creation
400	
401	**A user does not need to pre-create a tenant before signing up.** Self-registration automatically provisions a personal tenant in the same transaction. The user never sees the word "tenant" during signup — it happens silently in the background.
402	
403	#### Signup flow
404	
405	```
406	User fills in registration form (name, email, password)
407	  → RegistrationService.RegisterAsync(command)
408	      1. Creates ApplicationUser
409	      2. Creates Tenant (name = "{DisplayName}'s Workspace", editable later)
410	      3. Assigns user as TenantAdmin of the new tenant
411	      4. Sets ApplicationUser.TenantId = new tenant's TenantId
412	      5. Seeds default UserPreference rows (TimeZone = "UTC", MeasurementUnit = system default)
413	      6. Commits all in a single transaction
414	  → User is logged in, lands on their personal workspace
415	```
416	
417	`TenantId` is **never null** except for `SystemAdmin`. There is no "tenantless user" state. This keeps the Global Query Filter uniform — no special-casing for null anywhere in the codebase.
418	
419	#### Growing from solo to team
420	
421	Because every self-registered user already has a `Tenant` record, inviting a colleague is just adding another `ApplicationUser` to the same tenant — no data migration, no schema change. The user upgrades from solo to team invisibly.
422	
423	#### Tenant entity
424	
425	See full definition in §3.5 — `Tenant` includes `PlanId` for subscription gating.
426	
427	`TenantGuid` (not `TenantId`) is stored in the JWT claim and in Blazor's auth state — the `int` key never leaves the server.
428	
429	#### JWT claim strategy
430	
431	At login, both identifiers are written as claims so `ITenantContext` reads them without a DB lookup per request:
432	
433	```csharp
434	// Claims written at login
435	claims.Add(new Claim("tenant_guid", tenant.TenantGuid.ToString()));
436	claims.Add(new Claim("tenant_id",   tenant.TenantId.ToString()));   // int, for filter
437	```
438	
439	`ITenantContext` reads `tenant_id` (int) directly for all DB filtering. `tenant_guid` is available for display (e.g., admin UI showing which tenant a SystemAdmin is currently viewing).
440	
441	Also written as a claim at login:
442	
443	```csharp
444	claims.Add(new Claim("plan_id", tenant.PlanId.ToString())); // int PlanId, for plan gates
445	```
446	
447	This means `IPlanGateService` can check the plan from claims with no DB hit.
448	
449	### 3.5 Subscription Plans & Feature Gates
450	
451	A solo maker signs up and works entirely within a single-user experience — no tenant management UI is visible, no invite menus exist. If they later want to bring in employees or partners, they upgrade their plan and those tools unlock automatically. No data migration is required because the tenant record already exists.
452	
453	#### Plan Schema
454	
455	Plans use the same three-tier pattern as the material library — identity, temporal pricing detail, and EAV attributes — so adding or modifying a plan tier, changing pricing, or updating the feature bullet list on the marketing page requires no code changes, only data.
456	
457	```csharp
458	// Plan identity — system-level, not tenant-scoped

460	{
461	    public int PlanId { get; set; }
462	    public Guid PlanGuid { get; set; }
463	    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;         // internal: "Solo", "Team"
464	    public string Slug { get; set; } = string.Empty;         // url-safe: "solo", "team"
465	    public bool IsPubliclyVisible { get; set; }              // show on public pricing page
466	    public int SortOrder { get; set; }                       // left→right order on pricing page
467	    public virtual ICollection<PlanDetail> Details { get; set; } = new List<PlanDetail>();
468	    public virtual ICollection<PlanAttribute> Attributes { get; set; } = new List<PlanAttribute>();
469	}

471	// Temporal pricing + display record — one active row per plan at any instant
472	public class PlanDetail : CmEntityHistory   // EffectiveDate, ObsoleteDate — tracks price changes
473	{
474	    public int PlanDetailId { get; set; }
475	    public Guid PlanDetailGuid { get; set; }

501	#### `Tenant` entity (updated)
502	
503	```csharp
504	// Inherits CmEntity: CreatedDate, CreatedUserId, LastUpdatedDate, LastUpdatedUserId, RecordStateId
505	public class Tenant : CmEntity               // NOT ITenantScoped
506	{
507	    public int TenantId { get; set; }         // PK
508	    public Guid TenantGuid { get; set; }      // external reference (in JWT claim)
509	    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
510	    public string Slug { get; set; } = string.Empty;  // URL-safe, unique
511	    public bool IsActive { get; set; } = true;
512	    public int PlanId { get; set; }           // FK → Plan.PlanId
513	    public virtual Plan Plan { get; set; } = null!;

517	
518	#### `IPlanGateService`
519	
520	Defined in BRL. Code-level feature gating — checks whether a feature is available on the tenant's current plan. Reads `plan_id` from the JWT claim; no DB hit per request. The `PlanFeature` enum gates code paths; `PlanAttribute` drives what the marketing page displays — these are separate concerns.
521	
522	```csharp
523	public interface IPlanGateService
524	{
525	    bool IsEnabled(PlanFeature feature);  // reads plan_id from ITenantContext claim
526	}
527	
528	public enum PlanFeature
529	{
530	    MultiUserInvite,
531	    RoleManagement,
532	    TenantSettings,
533	    // future: AdvancedReporting, ApiAccess, etc.
534	}
535	```
536	
537	#### Blazor UI gating
538	
539	Features locked to a plan are wrapped in a `<PlanGate>` component (thin wrapper around `IPlanGateService`):
540	
541	```razor
542	<PlanGate Feature="PlanFeature.MultiUserInvite">
543	    <Authorized>
544	        <InviteUserButton />
545	    </Authorized>
546	    <Upgrade>
547	        <UpgradePlanCallToAction />   <!-- shown to Solo users in place of the button -->
548	    </Upgrade>
549	</PlanGate>
550	```
551	
552	Solo users see an "Upgrade to Team" prompt wherever team features would appear — they are never silently blocked without explanation.
553	
554	#### Plan upgrade flow
555	
556	**Phase 1–4 (current):** `SystemAdmin` flips `Tenant.PlanId` manually via the admin panel. No billing integration.
557	
558	**Future phase:** A self-service upgrade page where the tenant owner can change their own plan. Billing integration (e.g., Stripe) connects here. The core feature-gate logic does not change — only the mechanism that updates `PlanId` changes.
559	
560	#### Downgrade guard
561	
562	If a `Team` tenant attempts to downgrade to `Solo` while more than one active user exists, `PlanService.DowngradeAsync` returns a `Result.Failure` with a message listing the blocking users. The tenant must deactivate or remove the extra users before the downgrade is allowed.
563	
564	### 3.6 Role Hierarchy
565	
566	| Role | Scope | Capabilities |
567	|---|---|---|
568	| `SystemAdmin` | Platform-wide | Manage all tenants, change plan tiers, view all data, bypass filters, seed `CmTypeClass` and `CmType` tables. `TenantId = null`. |
569	| `TenantAdmin` | Within one tenant | Manage tenant users (Team plan only), configure material library and pricing. Auto-assigned on self-signup. |
570	| `TenantUser` | Within one tenant | Create/edit jobs, assemblies, and generate cut lists. |

572	## 5. Dictionary & Measurement System
573	
574	The system must be highly flexible, supporting dynamic conversions between metric and imperial systems based on user preference, while storing a canonical source of truth.
575	
576	### 4.1 System Dictionary Pattern
577	
578	The system uses a parent-child dictionary pattern for all enumerations, states, and classifications. The `BaseTypeBaseId` acts as the numeric floor. All domain entities link to specific records in `CmType` using a `{Description}TypeId` foreign key convention.
579	
580	```csharp
581	public class CmTypeClass : CmEntity
582	{
583	    public int CmTypeClassId { get; set; }         // PK
584	    public Guid CmTypeClassGuid { get; set; }      // external reference
585	    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
586	    public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
587	    public int BaseTypeId { get; set; }         // numeric floor e.g. 1000, 2000
588	    public virtual ICollection<CmType> Types { get; set; } = new List<CmType>();
589	}
590	
591	public class CmType : CmEntity
592	{
593	    public int CmTypeId { get; set; }               // PK e.g. 1001, 1002
594	    public Guid CmTypeGuid { get; set; }            // external reference
595	    public int CmTypeClassId { get; set; }          // FK → CmTypeClass.CmTypeClassId
596	    public virtual CmTypeClass TypeClass { get; set; } = null!;
597	    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
598	    public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
599	    public int Ordering { get; set; }               // display sort order within the class
600	    public int? TypeInt { get; set; }               // optional typed payload — integer value
601	    public string? TypeString { get; set; }         // optional typed payload — string value
602	    public decimal? TypeDecimal { get; set; }       // optional typed payload — decimal value
603	}
604	```

634	## 6. Core Domain Schema
635	
636	### 5.1 Material Library — System Base + Tenant Override Pattern
637	
638	The material library uses a **two-tier ownership model** with full temporal history at both tiers.
639	
640	#### Ownership Tiers
641	
642	| Tier | Entity | Owner | Tenant-Scoped |
643	|---|---|---|---|
644	| System base — identity | `Material` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
645	| System base — pricing history | `MaterialDetail` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
646	| System base — attributes (EAV) | `MaterialAttribute` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
647	| Tenant pricing history | `MaterialTenantDetail` | `TenantAdmin` | Yes |
648	| Tenant attribute overrides (EAV) | `MaterialTenantAttribute` | `TenantAdmin` | Yes |
649	
650	**Tenant-created materials** (no system counterpart) use the same tables but with `IsSystemMaterial = false` on `Material` and a `TenantId` set. All their `MaterialDetail` and `MaterialAttribute` rows are their own — they do not inherit from any system record.
651	
652	Effective library for a tenant = *system materials (with any tenant overrides applied)* + *tenant-created materials*.
653	
654	#### Schema
655	
656	```csharp
657	// System-owned — NOT ITenantScoped
658	public class Material : CmEntity
659	{
660	    public int MaterialId { get; set; }             // PK
661	    public Guid MaterialGuid { get; set; }          // external reference
662	    public bool IsSystemMaterial { get; set; }      // false = tenant-created
663	    public int? TenantId { get; set; }              // null when IsSystemMaterial = true
664	    public int MaterialCategoryTypeId { get; set; } // FK → CmType.CmTypeId
665	    public bool HasGrainDirection { get; set; }
666	    public ICollection<MaterialDetail> Details { get; set; }
667	    public ICollection<MaterialAttribute> Attributes { get; set; }
668	}
669	
670	// System temporal pricing chain — one row per pricing period
671	public class MaterialDetail : CmEntityHistory      // provides EffectiveDate, ObsoleteDate
672	{
673	    public int MaterialDetailId { get; set; }       // PK
674	    public Guid MaterialDetailGuid { get; set; }    // external reference
675	    public int MaterialId { get; set; }             // FK → Material.MaterialId
676	    public string Name { get; set; }
677	    public decimal UnitCost { get; set; }
678	    public decimal WasteFactorPercentage { get; set; }
679	}
680	
681	// System EAV attributes
682	public class MaterialAttribute : CmEntity
683	{
684	    public int MaterialAttributeId { get; set; }    // PK
685	    public Guid MaterialAttributeGuid { get; set; } // external reference
686	    public int MaterialId { get; set; }             // FK → Material.MaterialId
687	    public int AttributeTypeId { get; set; }        // FK → CmType.CmTypeId
688	    public int? CmMeasurementId { get; set; }       // FK → CmMeasurement.CmMeasurementId
689	    public string? StringValue { get; set; }
690	}
691	
692	// Tenant temporal pricing chain — one row per pricing period per tenant
693	// null override field = "not overridden, inherit from system"
694	public class MaterialTenantDetail : CmEntityHistory, ITenantScoped  // provides EffectiveDate, ObsoleteDate
695	{
696	    public int MaterialTenantDetailId { get; set; }     // PK
697	    public Guid MaterialTenantDetailGuid { get; set; }  // external reference
698	    public int TenantId { get; set; }                   // FK → Tenant.TenantId (int)
699	    public int MaterialId { get; set; }                 // FK → Material.MaterialId
700	    public bool IsHidden { get; set; }

702	    public decimal? OverrideUnitCost { get; set; }

704	}

706	// Tenant EAV attribute overrides — full replacement of a single attribute slot
707	public class MaterialTenantAttribute : CmEntityHistory, ITenantScoped  // provides EffectiveDate, ObsoleteDate
708	{

719	#### Resolution Rules (`MaterialResolutionService`)
720	
721	All resolution accepts an `asOfDate` parameter (defaults to `_timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime`). This enables historical pricing reports.
722	
723	**Pricing resolution** for a given material + tenant + date:
724	1. Find the active `MaterialTenantDetail` row (tenant, material, `EffectiveDate <= asOfDate`, `ObsoleteDate` null or `> asOfDate`).
725	2. If found: use it. For any nullable field that is null, fall back to the active system `MaterialDetail` value for the same date.
726	3. If not found: use the active system `MaterialDetail` row directly.
727	
728	**Attribute resolution** for a given material + tenant + date:
729	1. Start with all `MaterialAttribute` rows for the material (system set).
730	2. For each attribute slot (`AttributeTypeId`): if an active `MaterialTenantAttribute` exists for that tenant and date, replace the system value with the tenant value.
731	3. Tenant may also have `MaterialTenantAttribute` rows for attribute slots that don't exist in the system set — these are additive (tenant-only attributes).
732	
733	**System update propagation behavior:**
734	- Tenant has **no** `MaterialTenantDetail` row → system updates are immediately visible. Full system history is visible in reports.
735	- Tenant has a `MaterialTenantDetail` row with a specific field overridden → that field is frozen at the tenant's value. Other non-overridden fields still inherit system updates.
736	- Tenant can "reset a field to system" by setting the override field back to null.
737	- Tenant can "reset entirely" by deleting their `MaterialTenantDetail` rows.
738	
739	#### History & Reporting
740	
741	Because both tiers are temporal (effective/obsolete dates), reports can answer:
742	- "What did *we* pay for 3/4" maple plywood in Q3?" → query `MaterialTenantDetail` as-of Q3
743	- "What is the system reference price for that material in Q3?" → query `MaterialDetail` as-of Q3
744	- "Show me the price drift between system and our overrides over the last 12 months" → join both chains
745	
746	#### Temporal Succession Pattern
747	
748	All `*Detail` and `*Attribute` records — both system and tenant — follow the same succession contract:
749	
750	> For any given logical record key (e.g., `(TenantId, MaterialId, AttributeTypeId)`), exactly one row is active at any instant. The outgoing row's `ObsoleteDate` equals the incoming row's `EffectiveDate` — a shared boundary point with no gap and no overlap.
751	
752	```
753	Timeline ──────────────────────────────────────────────────▶
754	         |← Row A active ────────────|← Row B active ──────
755	         EffA                        ObsA == EffB
756	```
757	
758	**Succession operation** (handled atomically by `RecordSuccessionService`):
759	
760	1. Caller provides: the new record's data + an `effectiveAt` (`DateTime` UTC).
761	2. Service finds the currently active row for that key.
762	3. Sets `existing.ObsoleteDate = effectiveAt`.
763	4. Sets `newRecord.EffectiveDate = effectiveAt`, `newRecord.ObsoleteDate = null`.
764	5. Saves both in a single transaction.
765	
766	**Future-dated succession** (scheduled material change):
767	
768	```
769	Today (Oct 10):  Row A has ObsoleteDate = Nov 1 05:00 UTC
770	                 Row B has EffectiveDate = Nov 1 05:00 UTC, ObsoleteDate = null
771	
772	Before Nov 1:    Query resolves Row A  (ObsoleteDate > now)
773	After Nov 1:     Query resolves Row B  (EffectiveDate <= now, ObsoleteDate is null)
774	```
775	
776	The user entered "Nov 1 midnight Eastern" — the UI converted this to `2026-11-01T05:00:00+00:00` before sending the command. The server stores and queries UTC only.
777	
778	**Validation rules enforced by `RecordSuccessionService`:**
779	- `effectiveAt` must be ≥ `_timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime` minus a small grace window (prevents accidental back-dating).
780	- If a future-dated successor already exists, the new `effectiveAt` must be before the existing successor's `EffectiveDate` (no insertion into the middle of a chain without explicit intent).
781	- Gaps and overlaps are structurally prevented — the service is the only permitted write path for temporal records.
782	
783	**`RecordSuccessionService`** lives in BRL and is generic over any entity that implements `ITemporalRecord`:
784	
785	```csharp
786	public interface ITemporalRecord
787	{
788	    DateTime EffectiveDate { get; set; }     // mirrors CmEntityHistory — always UTC
789	    DateTime? ObsoleteDate { get; set; }
790	}
791	```
792	
793	`CmEntityHistory` already satisfies this interface structurally. Declaring it explicitly on `CmEntityHistory` allows `RecordSuccessionService` to work generically over any temporal entity.

863	### 5.4 Estimator
864	
865	Estimates are generated from the job hierarchy with zero required configuration — system defaults cover everything out of the box. Tenants tune the macro knobs (shop rate, markup) in their settings when they're ready for accuracy.
866	
867	#### Estimate math
868	
869	```
870	For each Part (× Quantity):
871	  Material cost  = sheet yield from CutLength × CutWidth
872	                   → MaterialResolutionService (as-of today) → unit cost × waste factor
873	  Operation time = Σ PartOperation.OperationType.TypeDecimal (hours/op seeded on CmType)
874	                   × Quantity
875	
876	Total material  = Σ all part material costs
877	Total hours     = Σ all part operation hours
878	Total labor     = Total hours × TenantSettings.ShopHourlyRate
879	Subtotal        = Total material + Total labor
880	Total           = Subtotal × (1 + TenantSettings.DefaultMarkupPercentage)
881	```
882	
883	Operation types (Dado, Dowel, Rabbet, Door Hang, etc.) are seeded as `CmType` records with `TypeDecimal` = estimated hours per operation. Tenants adjust their `TenantSettings` to reflect their actual shop speed and rates.
884

909	#### JobEstimate & JobEstimateLine
910	
911	Estimates are saved as versioned snapshots so the tenant can send v1 to a client, revise, send v2, and keep both on record. All rate values are snapshotted at generation time — changing `TenantSettings` later does not retroactively alter a saved estimate.
912	
913	Estimates follow a **draft → shipped** lifecycle. A draft is fully editable — generated values are starting points, not locked figures. Once shipped, the estimate becomes an immutable versioned record. A new revision starts a fresh draft generated from the current job state.
914	
915	```
916	GenerateAsync  →  Draft (no version, fully editable)
917	  ↓ user edits lines, adjusts costs, adds hardware/misc lines
918	ShipAsync      →  Sent (version stamped, locked — no further edits)
919	  ↓ need to revise?
920	GenerateAsync  →  new Draft (version = null, prior Sent records untouched)
921	```

960	#### TenantDiscountCode
961	
962	Tenant-created codes applied during estimate editing. The tenant controls all configuration — code string, discount type, value, expiry, and usage limits. Usage is tracked per shipped estimate (Draft applications do not count against limits).
963	
964	```csharp
965	public class TenantDiscountCode : CmEntity, ITenantScoped
966	{
967	    public int TenantDiscountCodeId { get; set; }    // PK
968	    public Guid TenantDiscountCodeGuid { get; set; } // external reference
969	    public int TenantId { get; set; }                // FK → Tenant.TenantId (int)
970	    public string Code { get; set; } = string.Empty; // unique per tenant — e.g. "SUMMER25"
971	    public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty; // appears on the estimate line
972	    public int DiscountTypeId { get; set; }          // FK → CmType (Percentage / FixedAmount)
973	    public virtual CmType DiscountType { get; set; } = null!;
974	    public decimal DiscountValue { get; set; }       // 0.10 = 10% off  |  50.00 = $50 off
975	    public DateTime? ExpiresAt { get; set; }         // UTC — null = no expiry
976	    public int? MaxUses { get; set; }                // null = unlimited
977	    public int UsageCount { get; set; }              // incremented by ShipAsync, decremented if Voided
978	}
979	```
980	
981	**Discount application rules:**
982	- Percentage discount: `TotalCost = -(estimate subtotal × DiscountValue)` — applied against the sum of all non-discount lines
983	- Fixed amount: `TotalCost = -DiscountValue`
984	- Multiple codes can be stacked on one estimate — each is its own `JobEstimateLine`
985	- `EstimatorService.ApplyDiscountAsync(estimateGuid, code)` looks up the code, validates it (not expired, under max uses), creates the discount line, and recalculates `JobEstimate.TotalCost`
986	- `UsageCount` is incremented in `ShipAsync` for every discount line on the estimate; decremented in `VoidAsync`
987	- Codes are validated against `ExpiresAt` and `MaxUses` at apply time — a code that was valid when applied but expires before shipping is still honoured (validation is at apply time, not ship time)
988	
989	**Editing rules:**
990	- Any field on `JobEstimateLine` is editable while `EstimateStatusTypeId == Draft`
991	- Lines can be added (hardware, misc, custom, discount) or removed while in Draft
992	- `JobEstimate.TotalCost` is recalculated as the sum of all `JobEstimateLine.TotalCost` on every save
993	- `EstimatorService.ShipAsync(estimateGuid)` flips status to Sent, assigns the next version number for that job, stamps `SentAt`, increments `UsageCount` on all applied discount codes — no edits permitted after this point
994	- `JobEstimateLine.TotalCost` is enforced server-side (`Quantity × UnitCost`) — the client sends `Quantity` and `UnitCost`, the server always recalculates `TotalCost`
995	
996	#### EstimatorService (BRL)
997	
998	| Method | Description |
999	|---|---|
1000	| `GenerateAsync(jobId)` | Creates a Draft estimate from current job state. Resolves materials via `MaterialResolutionService`, calculates sheet yield, sums operation hours from `CmType.TypeDecimal`, reads `TenantSettings` for rates. Returns `Result<Guid>`. |
1001	| `ApplyDiscountAsync(estimateGuid, code)` | Looks up code (must be Draft, not expired, under max uses), creates a Discount `JobEstimateLine`, recalculates total. Returns `Result<Guid>` (line Guid). |
1002	| `ShipAsync(estimateGuid)` | Locks estimate — stamps version, `SentAt`, increments `UsageCount` on all discount codes. Returns `Result<Guid>`. |
1003	| `VoidAsync(estimateGuid)` | Voids a Sent estimate — decrements `UsageCount` on all discount codes. Returns `Result<Guid>`. |

# CabinetMaker — Project Plan

**Date:** 2026-10-10

**Stack:** C# · Blazor Server · .NET 10 · Entity Framework Core 10 · MySQL (primary) / SQL Server (supported) · Bootstrap · Docker (Linux)

## 1. Project Purpose

CabinetMaker is a professional-grade, multi-tenant design tool for cabinet makers and furniture builders. Its core job is to capture, organize, and calculate measurements for cabinet projects — from a single unit to a complete kitchen or custom furniture piece — and produce accurate cut lists, material estimates, and project summaries.

Two foundational primitives underpin everything else:

1. A **database-driven, unit-agnostic measurement system** — every dimension, mass, or volume flows through a unified conversion engine, preventing metric/imperial collisions and supporting tape-measure-accurate fractional snapping.

2. A **tenant isolation model** — every piece of data is scoped to the tenant it belongs to, enforced at the database layer, invisible to application code.

## 2. Infrastructure & Deployment

### 2.1 Docker / Linux Hosting

The application is packaged as a Docker container and can run on any Linux Docker host (self-hosted, VPS, cloud VM). No Azure-specific or Windows-specific dependencies are permitted.

```
docker-compose.yml (development)
  web       — CabinetMaker.Web container (port 8080)
  db        — MySQL 8.x container (port 3306)

Dockerfile  (multi-stage)
  Stage 1 (build): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:10.0
  Stage 2 (runtime): mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0-bookworm-slim
```

All configuration (connection strings, admin seed credentials) is supplied via environment variables. No secrets are baked into the image.

Two compose files are maintained:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | Local development — builds from source, exposes all ports, ships with safe dev defaults, includes dbgate DB admin UI on port 8081 |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | Production — pulls a pre-built registry image, binds web to `127.0.0.1:8080` only, no default passwords, `restart: always`, no DB admin UI |

### 2.1.1 Production Reverse Proxy

In production the app sits behind an existing nginx reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager or equivalent). The app container binds only to `127.0.0.1:8080` — it is never directly internet-facing. The proxy handles SSL termination, domain assignment, and certificate management. Deploying a new version is: push image to registry → pull on server → `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d` → register the `127.0.0.1:8080` upstream in the proxy console. No nginx container is included in the production compose file.

### 2.2 Database Provider Abstraction

**Primary: MySQL 8.x** (Oracle official `MySql.EntityFrameworkCore` provider). **Also supported: SQL Server** (Microsoft EF Core provider). The active provider is selected at startup from a single config value:

```
# appsettings.json / environment variable
"DatabaseProvider": "MySql"   // or "SqlServer"
```

A `DatabaseProviderFactory` extension method in DAL registers the correct `DbContextOptions` based on this value:

```csharp
// DAL/Extensions/DatabaseProviderExtensions.cs
services.AddDbContext<CabinetMakerDbContext>(options =>
{
    if (provider == "MySql")
        options.UseMySQL(connectionString);
    else
        options.UseSqlServer(connectionString);
});
```

**Provider differences to account for:**

| Feature | MySQL (Pomelo) | SQL Server |
|---|---|---|
| JSON columns | `JSON` type, `.HasColumnType("json")` | `nvarchar(max)` or `json` (SQL Server 2022+) |
| GUIDs | `char(36)` or `binary(16)` | `uniqueidentifier` |
| Auto-increment | `AUTO_INCREMENT` | `IDENTITY` |
| Migrations | Separate migration sets per provider, or provider-aware migrations |

Migrations are kept in separate folders: `DAL/Migrations/MySql/` and `DAL/Migrations/SqlServer/`. A CLI helper script selects the correct migration context at design time.

### 2.3 Timezone Architecture

All temporal data in the system must be unambiguous about which instant in time it refers to. This matters especially for future-dated succession records (§5.1) where a user schedules a material change to take effect "at midnight on Nov 1" — midnight in *whose* timezone needs a definitive answer.

#### Rule: UTC everywhere in the database and server

- **Database:** All `DATETIME` columns store UTC values. The DB server timezone is irrelevant and must never influence stored values. MySQL `TIMESTAMP` type is specifically avoided because it auto-converts using the server timezone — `DATETIME` is used instead.
- **C# domain model:** All temporal properties use `DateTime`, always in UTC. The convention is enforced at the service boundary — every value written to a `DateTime` field must be UTC. Reading from DB always returns UTC. `DateTime.Now` is never used anywhere in the codebase.
- **EF Core convention:** A global value converter enforces `DateTimeKind.Utc` on all `DateTime` properties at the DbContext boundary, converting any non-UTC value on read and throwing on write if `Kind != Utc`.
- **Server-side "now":** All services obtain the current instant through an injected `TimeProvider`. Never call `DateTime.UtcNow` or `DateTime.Now` directly.

```csharp
// Production — registered once in Program.cs
services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);

// In any service that needs the current time
public class RecordSuccessionService(TimeProvider timeProvider)
{
    private DateTime Now => _timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime;
}
```

Using `TimeProvider` makes every service that touches time fully testable — `FakeTimeProvider` (from `Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing`) lets tests set and advance the clock without any static manipulation.

#### Rule: User timezone stays in the UI layer

The server and BRL services are timezone-unaware. They only speak UTC. Conversion happens at the edges:

```
User types "Nov 1 midnight"
  → UI reads user's IANA timezone from preference (e.g., "America/New_York")
  → UI converts: Nov 1 00:00 America/New_York → 2026-11-01 05:00:00 UTC
  → Command sent to BRL carries the UTC DateTime
  → Stored in DB as UTC DATETIME

DB returns 2026-11-01 05:00:00 (UTC)
  → UI converts back to America/New_York → displays "Nov 1 12:00 AM"
```

#### User Timezone Preference

Each `ApplicationUser` stores an IANA timezone identifier (e.g., `America/New_York`, `Europe/London`, `America/Los_Angeles`). Windows timezone names are explicitly not used — IANA identifiers are portable across Linux containers.

If a user has not set a timezone preference, the Blazor app captures the browser's IANA timezone via a one-time JS interop call on session start and uses it as the session default (without persisting it):

```javascript
// Called once on circuit connect
Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone  // → "America/Chicago"
```

#### Timezone Conversion Service

`ITimezoneService` is defined in BRL. The Web project provides the implementation using `NodaTime` (which correctly handles DST transitions, historical offset changes, and all IANA timezone rules):

```csharp
public interface ITimezoneService
{
    DateTime ToUtc(DateTime localDateTime, string ianaTimezoneId);
    DateTime ToLocal(DateTime utcValue, string ianaTimezoneId);
    string GetUserTimezone(); // reads from current user claim or session default
}
```

`NodaTime` is added only to the **Web** project (display concerns). Domain and BRL remain free of any NodaTime dependency — they only ever hold `DateTime` values in UTC.

#### DST Transition Edge Cases

DST transitions produce two distinct failure modes that require explicit handling. Both are **UI input problems only** — once a value is stored as UTC the succession logic is completely DST-immune.

**Case 1 — Gap (spring forward):** Clocks jump forward (e.g., 2:00 AM → 3:00 AM on March 8 in US/Central). The hour 2:00–3:00 AM does not exist. Any local time in that window is invalid.

**Case 2 — Overlap (fall back):** Clocks fall back (e.g., 2:00 AM → 1:00 AM on Nov 1 in US/Central). The hour 1:00–2:00 AM occurs twice. "1:30 AM Nov 1" is ambiguous — it could be 1:30 AM CDT (UTC−5) or 1:30 AM CST (UTC−6), two different UTC instants 60 minutes apart.

NodaTime's `DateTimeZone.MapLocal(LocalDateTime)` returns a `ZoneLocalMapping` that explicitly identifies which case applies:

```csharp
var zone = DateTimeZoneProviders.Tzdb[ianaTimezoneId];
var mapping = zone.MapLocal(localDateTime);

switch (mapping.Count)
{
    case 1:
        // Unambiguous — normal case
        return mapping.Single().ToDateTimeUtc().ToDateTimeUnspecified(); // DateTime UTC

    case 0:
        // GAP: this local time does not exist (spring forward)
        // Do not silently snap — surface to the user
        throw new SkippedTimeException(localDateTime, zone);

    case 2:
        // OVERLAP: this local time exists twice (fall back)
        // Do not silently pick one — surface to the user
        throw new AmbiguousTimeException(localDateTime, zone,
            mapping.First().ToDateTimeUtc(),   // earlier (daylight) as UTC DateTime
            mapping.Last().ToDateTimeUtc());   // later (standard) as UTC DateTime
}
```

**UI behavior for each case:**

| Case | What the user sees | Suggested default |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | Nothing — input accepted, converted to UTC silently | — |
| Gap (spring forward) | Inline warning: *"This time doesn't exist — clocks skip from [before] to [after] on this date. Use [time before gap] or [time after gap]?"* with two buttons | Snap forward (post-gap) |
| Overlap (fall back) | Inline warning: *"This time occurs twice due to the clock change. Which did you mean — [offset 1] or [offset 2]?"* with two buttons showing explicit UTC offsets | Standard time (later occurrence) |

Both warnings are handled in the `DateTimeInput` Blazor component. The component emits a resolved UTC `DateTime` only after the ambiguity is cleared.

**Why succession records are DST-immune once stored:**

The temporal query `EffectiveDate <= queryInstant && (ObsoleteDate == null || ObsoleteDate > queryInstant)` runs entirely in UTC. UTC has no clock changes — every instant is unique and unambiguous. No "blocking out" strategy is needed, unlike recurring scheduled tasks which must deal with DST on every firing.

The recurring-scheduler problem arises because a rule like "run at 2:00 AM every day" has to be re-evaluated each day against a potentially shifting local clock. Succession records have no such rule — they are one-time point-in-time events fully resolved to UTC at the moment of creation.

#### Why This Avoids the Common Pitfalls

| Pitfall | How this design avoids it |
|---|---|
| Spring-forward gap: user enters a non-existent time | `ZoneLocalMapping.Count == 0` detected; UI shows disambiguation — never silently snapped |
| Fall-back overlap: user enters an ambiguous time | `ZoneLocalMapping.Count == 2` detected; UI shows both UTC offsets for user to choose |
| Recurring task fires twice on fall-back | Not applicable — successions are one-time events, not recurring rules |
| MySQL server timezone contamination | `DATETIME` type (not `TIMESTAMP`) — MySQL never auto-converts |
| `DateTime.Kind.Unspecified` written to DB | EF global value converter enforces `DateTimeKind.Utc` on all `DateTime` properties — throws on write if Kind is not Utc |
| Future date stored in wrong timezone | User input always converted to UTC in UI before leaving the browser context |
| Reporting across timezones | All report queries run in UTC; display layer converts per-user |

## 3. Solution Structure

```
CabinetMaker.slnx
└── src/
    ├── CabinetMaker.Domain/         # EF entities + base classes — private to DAL
    ├── CabinetMaker.Domain.Shared/  # POCOs, repository interfaces, Result<T>, Mapperly mappers
    ├── CabinetMaker.DAL/            # EF DbContext, migrations, repository implementations
    ├── CabinetMaker.BRL/            # Business rules, services, validation
    └── CabinetMaker.Web/            # Blazor Server UI, ViewModels (MVVM)

# Future phase — added only when MAUI client is built:
#   CabinetMaker.API/               # GraphQL API (Hot Chocolate) — thin layer over BRL
#   CabinetMaker.MAUI/              # .NET MAUI client — calls API via GraphQL
```

### Project Dependency Flow

```
Web  ──────────────────────────────────► Domain.Shared
 │                                            ▲
 ▼                                            │
BRL  ──────────────────────────────────► Domain.Shared
 │                                            ▲
 ▼                                            │
DAL  ──► Domain (EF entities)  ──────► Domain.Shared
```

| Project | References | Never references |
|---|---|---|
| `Domain` | *(none)* | Everything else |
| `Domain.Shared` | *(none)* | Everything else |
| `DAL` | `Domain` + `Domain.Shared` | `BRL`, `Web` |
| `BRL` | `Domain.Shared` only | `Domain`, `DAL` directly |
| `Web` | `BRL` + `Domain.Shared` | `Domain`, `DAL` directly |

`Domain` is completely invisible above the DAL boundary. BRL and Web never import an EF entity type. DAL repositories accept and return only `Domain.Shared` POCOs — the EF entity is an internal implementation detail of the repository method.

### What lives in each project

**`Domain`** — EF entity classes, `CmEntity` / `CmEntityHistory` base classes. Nothing else.

**`Domain.Shared`** — everything the upper layers need to work with:
- **POCOs** — plain classes mirroring entity data shapes, no base class, no EF attributes. **POCOs expose `{TableName}Guid` only — the `int {TableName}Id` is stripped at the DAL boundary and never reaches BRL or Web.** All POCO-to-POCO references use `Guid` properties.
- **Repository interfaces** — `IProjectRepository`, `IMaterialRepository`, etc.; all signatures use POCO types
- **Service interfaces** — `ITimezoneService`, `IPlanGateService`, etc.
- **`Result<T>`** — the success/failure discriminated union used throughout BRL
- **Shared enums** — `PlanFeature`, `RecordState`, `PlanType`
- **Mapperly POCO→POCO mappers** — for any cross-POCO transformations needed in BRL or Web

**`DAL`** — EF `DbContext`, repository implementations, migrations, and **Mapperly Entity→POCO mappers**. This is the only project that ever sees both an EF entity and its POCO counterpart. The mapper runs just before a repository method returns.

### Mapperly — Entity → POCO mapping

[Mapperly](https://mapperly.riok.app/) (`Riok.Mapperly`) is a source generator: you declare a partial mapper class and it emits the full mapping method body at compile time. Zero reflection, no runtime overhead, and mapping errors surface at build time.

```csharp
// DAL/Mappers/MaterialMapper.cs
[Mapper]
public partial class MaterialMapper
{
    public partial MaterialPoco ToMaterial(Material entity);
    public partial Material ToEntity(MaterialPoco poco);

    // Collections handled automatically
    public partial List<MaterialPoco> ToMaterialList(IEnumerable<Material> entities);
}
```

The mapper in DAL is also responsible for the int→Guid promotion: the entity carries both `{TableName}Id` and `{TableName}Guid`, but the generated POCO only receives the `Guid`. The `int` key never leaves the DAL.

- Entity→POCO mappers live in **DAL** (only project with access to both types)
- POCO→POCO mappers (e.g., flattening for a report view) live in **Domain.Shared**
- Mapperly is added to **both** `Domain.Shared` and `DAL` as a source-generator-only reference:

```xml
<PackageReference Include="Riok.Mapperly" Version="x.x.x"
                  PrivateAssets="all" IncludeAssets="analyzers;build" />
```

`PrivateAssets="all"` means the generator runs at build time but adds no runtime DLL dependency — the output is just the generated C# code.

## 4. Multi-Tenancy & Identity Architecture

### 3.1 Isolation Model — Row-Level with Global Query Filters

**Choice: single database, shared schema, `TenantId` discriminator column on every tenant-scoped table.**
EF Core Global Query Filters enforce isolation at the ORM layer. No query in the application ever accidentally crosses tenant boundaries.

### 3.2 Base Classes & Key Naming Convention

All entities inherit from one of two base classes defined in `CabinetMaker.Domain`:

**`CmEntity`** — standard base for all non-temporal entities:

```csharp
// CabinetMaker.Domain/Entities/CmEntity.cs
public class CmEntity
{
    public DateTime CreatedDate { get; set; }       // UTC — set on insert
    public int CreatedUserId { get; set; }          // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
    public DateTime? LastUpdatedDate { get; set; }  // UTC — set on every update
    public int? LastUpdatedUserId { get; set; }     // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
    public int RecordStateId { get; set; }          // FK → CmType (Active/Inactive/Deleted)
}
```

**`CmEntityHistory`** — base for all temporal (succession-pattern) entities:

```csharp
// CabinetMaker.Domain/Entities/CmEntityHistory.cs
public class CmEntityHistory : CmEntity
{
    public DateTime EffectiveDate { get; set; }     // UTC — when this record becomes active
    public DateTime? ObsoleteDate { get; set; }     // UTC — when this record is superseded
}
```

All `DateTime` fields in both classes are **always UTC**. `DateTime.Now` and `DateTime.UtcNow` are never called directly — the current time is always obtained from an injected `TimeProvider` via `_timeProvider.GetUtcNow().DateTime`.

**Key naming on top of the base classes:**

Every entity declares its own named PK and external Guid — the base class does not define them because the name must match the table:

| Property | Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `{TableName}Id` | `int` (auto-increment PK) | Internal DB joins — never exposed in URLs or API responses |
| `{TableName}Guid` | `Guid` (unique index) | External identifier — used in all UI routes, links, and exports |

`{TableName}Guid` is generated server-side (`Guid.NewGuid()`) in `SaveChangesAsync` on insert — never supplied by the client.

### 3.3 Tenant-Scoped Entities

Every entity that belongs to a tenant implements the marker interface. `TenantId` is an `int` FK to `Tenant.TenantId` — all joins use the int key, not the Guid.

```csharp
public interface ITenantScoped
{
    int TenantId { get; set; }   // FK → Tenant.TenantId (int)
}
```

Entities that are **not** tenant-scoped: `Tenant`, `ApplicationUser`, and System Dictionaries (`CmTypeClass`, `CmType`, `CmUnit`).

### 3.3.1 ApplicationUser

ASP.NET Core Identity does not allow renaming the `Id` property, so `ApplicationUser` is an exception to the `{TableName}Id` convention — it retains Identity's `int Id`. A `Guid ApplicationUserGuid` serves the same external-reference purpose.

```csharp
public class ApplicationUser : IdentityUser<int>   // int PK via Identity
{
    public Guid UserGuid { get; set; }             // external reference
    public int? TenantId { get; set; }             // null = SystemAdmin; FK → Tenant.TenantId
    public string DisplayName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
}
```

Display preferences (timezone, measurement units) live in `UserPreferences` — not on the Identity table.

### 3.3.2 UserPreference

A one-to-many collection of key-value preference rows per user. Adding a new preference type (theme, language, date format, etc.) requires only a new `CmType` seed record — no schema change ever needed.

```csharp
public class UserPreference : CmEntity
{
    public int UserPreferenceId { get; set; }       // PK
    public Guid UserPreferenceGuid { get; set; }    // external reference
    public int UserId { get; set; }                 // FK → ApplicationUser.Id
    public int PreferenceTypeId { get; set; }       // FK → CmType (TimeZone / MeasurementUnit / Theme / etc.)
    public virtual CmType PreferenceType { get; set; } = null!;
    public int? TypeInt { get; set; }               // integer preference value
    public string? TypeString { get; set; }         // string preference value
    public decimal? TypeDecimal { get; set; }       // decimal preference value
}
```

Each preference is one row. Examples:

| `PreferenceType` (`CmType`) | Value field | Example value |
|---|---|---|
| `TimeZone` | `TypeString` | `"America/New_York"` |
| `MeasurementUnit` | `TypeInt` | CmUnitId for inches |
| `Theme` | `TypeString` | `"dark"` |
| `DateFormat` | `TypeString` | `"MM/dd/yyyy"` |

At registration, `RegistrationService` seeds the two default rows (`TimeZone = "UTC"`, `MeasurementUnit = null` / system default). All preference rows for a user are loaded once at login and written as claims so the Web layer reads them without a DB hit per request:

```csharp
foreach (var pref in userPreferences)
    claims.Add(new Claim($"pref_{pref.PreferenceType.Name}", pref.TypeString ?? pref.TypeInt?.ToString() ?? ""));
```

### 3.4 User Signup & Tenant Auto-Creation

**A user does not need to pre-create a tenant before signing up.** Self-registration automatically provisions a personal tenant in the same transaction. The user never sees the word "tenant" during signup — it happens silently in the background.

#### Signup flow

```
User fills in registration form (name, email, password)
  → RegistrationService.RegisterAsync(command)
      1. Creates ApplicationUser
      2. Creates Tenant (name = "{DisplayName}'s Workspace", editable later)
      3. Assigns user as TenantAdmin of the new tenant
      4. Sets ApplicationUser.TenantId = new tenant's TenantId
      5. Seeds default UserPreference rows (TimeZone = "UTC", MeasurementUnit = system default)
      6. Commits all in a single transaction
  → User is logged in, lands on their personal workspace
```

`TenantId` is **never null** except for `SystemAdmin`. There is no "tenantless user" state. This keeps the Global Query Filter uniform — no special-casing for null anywhere in the codebase.

#### Growing from solo to team

Because every self-registered user already has a `Tenant` record, inviting a colleague is just adding another `ApplicationUser` to the same tenant — no data migration, no schema change. The user upgrades from solo to team invisibly.

#### Tenant entity

See full definition in §3.5 — `Tenant` includes `PlanId` for subscription gating.

`TenantGuid` (not `TenantId`) is stored in the JWT claim and in Blazor's auth state — the `int` key never leaves the server.

#### JWT claim strategy

At login, both identifiers are written as claims so `ITenantContext` reads them without a DB lookup per request:

```csharp
// Claims written at login
claims.Add(new Claim("tenant_guid", tenant.TenantGuid.ToString()));
claims.Add(new Claim("tenant_id",   tenant.TenantId.ToString()));   // int, for filter
```

`ITenantContext` reads `tenant_id` (int) directly for all DB filtering. `tenant_guid` is available for display (e.g., admin UI showing which tenant a SystemAdmin is currently viewing).

Also written as a claim at login:

```csharp
claims.Add(new Claim("plan_id", tenant.PlanId.ToString())); // int PlanId, for plan gates
```

This means `IPlanGateService` can check the plan from claims with no DB hit.

### 3.5 Subscription Plans & Feature Gates

A solo maker signs up and works entirely within a single-user experience — no tenant management UI is visible, no invite menus exist. If they later want to bring in employees or partners, they upgrade their plan and those tools unlock automatically. No data migration is required because the tenant record already exists.

#### `IPlanGateService`

If a `Team` tenant attempts to downgrade to `Solo` while more than one active user exists, `PlanService.DowngradeAsync` returns a `Result.Failure` with a message listing the blocking users. The tenant must deactivate or remove the extra users before the downgrade is allowed.

| Role | Scope | Capabilities |

## 6. Core Domain Schema

### 5.1 Material Library — System Base + Tenant Override Pattern

The material library uses a **two-tier ownership model** with full temporal history at both tiers.

#### Ownership Tiers

| Tier | Entity | Owner | Tenant-Scoped |
|---|---|---|---|
| System base — identity | `Material` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
| System base — pricing history | `MaterialDetail` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
| System base — attributes (EAV) | `MaterialAttribute` | `SystemAdmin` | No |
| Tenant pricing history | `MaterialTenantDetail` | `TenantAdmin` | Yes |
| Tenant attribute overrides (EAV) | `MaterialTenantAttribute` | `TenantAdmin` | Yes |

**Tenant-created materials** (no system counterpart) use the same tables but with `IsSystemMaterial = false` on `Material` and a `TenantId` set. All their `MaterialDetail` and `MaterialAttribute` rows are their own — they do not inherit from any system record.

Effective library for a tenant = *system materials (with any tenant overrides applied)* + *tenant-created materials*.

#### Schema
